extracted.intended_audience: employers/petitioners, law_enforcement_agencies (LEAs), USCIS officers, and immigration practitioners advising on S and CW-1/CW-2 classifications
extracted.subtask_short: USCIS CW-1/CW-2 and S visa rules
extracted.subtask_description: Federal regulatory standards and procedural requirements for S nonimmigrant classification and CNMI-only CW-1/CW-2 transitional worker petitions, including definitions, evidentiary requirements, employer/LEA responsibilities, numerical caps, petition/approval/denial processes, and conditions of status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assistant Attorney General certification requirements for S classification
rubrics_metrics.description: The certification of the Assistant Attorney General, Criminal Division, to the Commissioner recommending approval of the application for S nonimmigrant classification shall contain the following: (1) All information and attachments that may constitute, or relate to, a ground or grounds of excludability under section 212(a) of the Act; (2) Each section of law under which the alien appears to be inadmissible; (3) The reasons that waiver(s) of inadmissibility are considered to be justifiable and in the national interest; (4) A detailed statement that the alien is eligible for S nonimmigrant classification, explaining the nature of the alien's cooperation with the government and the government's need for the alien's presence in the United States; (5) The intended date of arrival; (6) The length of the proposed stay in the United States; (7) The purpose of the proposed stay; and (8) A statement that the application falls within the statutorily specified numerical limitation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certification must include all listed items; these form the basis for the Commissioner's review and any waiver of inadmissibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advisory panel composition and function for S classification
rubrics_metrics.description: Where necessary, an advisory panel composed of representatives of the Service, U.S. Marshals Service, FBI, DEA, Criminal Division, Department of State, and other LEAs (including state and federal courts designated by the Attorney General) will review completed applications and submit a recommendation to the Assistant Attorney General, Criminal Division.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Panel's function is to prioritize cases in light of numerical limitations to determine which cases are forwarded to the Commissioner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission of certified S requests to Service
rubrics_metrics.description: The Assistant Attorney General, Criminal Division, shall forward to the Commissioner only qualified applications for S-5 classification that are certified in accordance with the regulation and fall within the annual numerical limitation; similarly for S-6 when also certified by the Secretary of State for S-6 eligibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only certified and numerically-eligible requests are forwarded to USCIS/Commissioner for final action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delegation of waiver authority and Commissioner's decision on S applications
rubrics_metrics.description: The Attorney General's authority to waive grounds of excludability pursuant to section 212 is delegated to the Commissioner and shall be exercised with regard to S classification only upon certification of the Assistant Attorney General, Criminal Division. Such certification is nonreviewable as to significance/importance/ worthwhileness to law enforcement. The Commissioner makes the final decision to approve or deny.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certification's factual/strategic determinations are nonreviewable; Commissioner acts on certification to approve/deny.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approval notification and admission period for S classification
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon approval of the application on Form I-854, the Commissioner shall notify the Assistant Attorney General, Criminal Division, the Secretary of State, and Service officers as appropriate. Admission shall be authorized for a period not to exceed 3 years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approval triggers notifications to relevant agencies and limits admission period to up to three years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Denial procedure and nonappealability for S classification
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Commissioner denies an application for S classification on Form I-854, the Assistant Attorney General, Criminal Division, and relevant LEA shall be notified. The AAG shall concur or object; absence of objection within 7 days is deemed concurrence. If AAG objects, the matter is referred to the Deputy Attorney General for final resolution. The alien and LEA have no right of appeal from any decision to deny.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Denial involves internal interagency concurrence/objection timeline; no appeal by alien or LEA is permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission to Secretary of State for S visa
rubrics_metrics.description: No request for S nonimmigrant visa classification may be presented to the Secretary of State unless it is approved and forwarded by the Commissioner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consular visa action for S classification requires prior USCIS/Commissioner approval and forwarding.

rubrics_metrics.name: S nonimmigrant conditions of status — alien responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: An alien witness or informant must certify and fulfill terms on Form I-854. The alien must: (A) report quarterly to the LEA on whereabouts and activities and as otherwise specified on Form I-854; (B) notify the LEA of any change of home or work address, phone numbers, or travel plans; (C) abide by the law and all specified terms, limitations, or restrictions on the visa/Form I-854/waivers; and (D) cooperate with the responsible LEA in accordance with the terms and any restrictions on Form I-854.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compliance with reporting, notification, lawful behavior, and cooperation obligations is a condition of maintaining S status.

rubrics_metrics.name: S nonimmigrant conditions of status — LEA responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: The LEA that assumes responsibility must: (ii) provide the Assistant Attorney General with the name of the control agent on an ongoing basis and provide a quarterly report indicating whereabouts, activities, and other control information; (iii) report immediately to the Service any failure by the alien to report quarterly, cooperate, comply with S terms, or refrain from criminal activity (information also forwarded to AAG); (iv) report annually to the AAG on whether the alien's classification and cooperation resulted in a successful prosecution/investigation or prevention/frustration of terrorist acts; and (v) assist the alien in applying for employment authorization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: LEAs have ongoing reporting and monitoring obligations and must notify government actors of compliance failures and outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employment authorization for S nonimmigrants
rubrics_metrics.description: An alien classified under section 101(a)(15)(S) may apply for employment authorization by filing Form I-765, Application for Employment Authorization, with fee, in accordance with the instructions on that form pursuant to § 274a.12(c)(21).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employment authorization is obtained through standard I-765 process and specific regulatory subsection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to maintain S status and deportation procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: An S-classified alien shall abide by all terms and conditions imposed. If terms will not be or have not been met, or have been violated, or if alien is convicted of a crime punishable by 1 year+ imprisonment, or otherwise rendered deportable, the Commissioner shall proceed to deport pursuant to 8 CFR 242.26. If deportation is decided, AAG and LEA are notified; AAG shall concur or object within 7 days or be deemed to concur; if AAG objects, refer to Deputy AG. Alien and LEA have no right of appeal from deportation decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Violations or serious criminal convictions can lead to deportation; interagency concurrence process applies but no appeal rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Change of classification rules for S nonimmigrants
rubrics_metrics.description: (i) An alien in S classification is prohibited from changing to any other nonimmigrant classification. (ii) An LEA may request that any alien lawfully admitted and maintaining status under § 248.1 (except those in § 248.2) have their classification changed to S per § 248.3(h).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Changing out of S status is generally prohibited, but LEA-initiated change-requests to S classification are governed by separate provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions applicable to CW-1 petitions — ‘CW-1 Application for Temporary Employment Certification’
rubrics_metrics.description: CW-1 Application for Temporary Employment Certification means OMB-approved Form ETA-9142C (or successor) and appendices, a valid prevailing wage determination (Form ETA-9141C or successor), and supporting documentation submitted by an employer to secure a temporary labor certification determination from DOL's OFLC as set in 20 CFR 655.420–655.422.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies required DOL forms and supporting documentation that constitute the TLC application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions — ‘Direct Guam transit’
rubrics_metrics.description: Direct Guam transit means travel from the CNMI to a foreign place by an alien in CW status, or from a foreign place to the CNMI by an alien with a valid CW visa, on a direct itinerary involving a flight stopover or connection in Guam (and no other place).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows limited Guam transit without being treated as travel to the rest of the U.S. for CW status purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions — ‘Doing business’
rubrics_metrics.description: Doing business means the regular, systematic, and continuous provision of goods or services by an employer and does not include the mere presence of an agent or office of the employer in the CNMI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes substantive presence/activity threshold for employer eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions — ‘Employer’
rubrics_metrics.description: Employer means a person, firm, corporation, contractor, or other association or organization which (A) engages a person to work within the CNMI; and (B) has or will have an employer-employee relationship with the CW-1 nonimmigrant being petitioned for.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines which entities may petition as employers for CW-1 workers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions — ‘Employer-employee relationship’
rubrics_metrics.description: Employer-employee relationship means that the employer will hire, pay, fire, supervise, and control the work of the employee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists the control/authority indicators used to determine whether an employment relationship exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions — ‘Lawfully present in the CNMI’
rubrics_metrics.description: Lawfully present in the CNMI means the alien was lawfully admitted or paroled into the CNMI under immigration laws on or after the transition program effective date (excluding certain B-1/B-2, visa-free, or specific parolees) and remains in lawful immigration status or authorized parole period has not expired.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies which on-island presences qualify as lawful for petition purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions — ‘Legitimate business’ criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Legitimate business, as determined by DHS, means a real, active, operating commercial or entrepreneurial undertaking that: (A) produces services or goods for profit, or is a government/charitable/nonprofit; (B) meets applicable legal requirements for doing business in the CNMI; (C) has substantially complied with wage/hour, OSHA, nondiscrimination, and other employment-related requirements during the five years preceding the petition and continues substantial compliance; (D) does not engage in or knowingly benefit from prostitution, human trafficking, or other illegal activity; (E) is a participant in good standing in E-Verify; (F) does not have certain disqualified individuals as owners/investors/managers involved (with specific five-year lookback rules); and (G) is not a successor in interest to an undertaking that has not complied with (C) or (D).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets a multi-factor compliance and legitimacy standard for employers seeking to petition for CW-1 workers; includes lookback periods and prohibition on benefiting from illegal activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions — ‘Long-term worker’ and ‘Minor child’
rubrics_metrics.description: Long-term worker means an alien admitted as CW-1 during FY2015 and during each of FY2016–2018. Minor child means a child under 18 as defined in section 101(b)(1) of the Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines categories with specific impacts on petition validity and eligibility rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions — ‘Numerical limitation’ and reservations
rubrics_metrics.description: Numerical limitation means the maximum number of persons who may be granted CW-1 status in a fiscal year; specific yearly caps are listed for FY2018 through first quarter FY2030 (e.g., 9,998 for 2018, down to 1,000 for Q1 FY2030). Within the caps DHS reserves numbers for specified occupational categories (e.g., 200 for healthcare occupations, 60 for certain public utilities occupations) and may adjust reservations via Federal Register notice based on demand, unused numbers, recommendations, etc. Unused numbers do not carry over; petitions that would meet a cap will be rejected when cap met; revocations can increase next year's cap numerically per rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Numerical caps and reservations are strictly applied; DHS can adjust reservations and will cease processing cap-subject petitions once cap met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions — ‘Occupational category’
rubrics_metrics.description: Occupational category means employment activities DHS determined require alien workers to supplement the resident workforce and includes enumerated groups (professional/technical/management; clerical/sales; service; agricultural/fisheries/forestry; processing; machine trade; benchwork; structural work; miscellaneous).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies the occupational groupings used for eligibility and reservations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions — ‘Participant in good standing in the E-Verify program’
rubrics_metrics.description: Participant in good standing means an employer enrolled in E-Verify for all U.S. hiring sites at time of filing; in compliance with E-Verify requirements including verifying employment eligibility of newly hired employees; and continues to be in good standing while employing any CW-1 nonimmigrant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employer E-Verify participation is a continuing compliance requirement for eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions — ‘Petition’
rubrics_metrics.description: Petition means USCIS Form I-129CW (or successor), any supplemental information requested by USCIS, and additional evidence as may be prescribed or requested by USCIS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies the form and supporting materials that constitute a CW petition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions — ‘Successor in interest’ factors
rubrics_metrics.description: Successor in interest means an employer controlling and carrying on the business of a previous employer; factors considered (no one factor dispositive) include substantial continuity of operations; use of same facilities; continuity of workforce; similarity of jobs/conditions; similarity of supervisory personnel; whether former management retains interest; similarity in machinery/equipment/production methods; similarity of products/services; and ability of predecessor to provide relief.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists non-exhaustive factors DHS considers when determining successor liability or status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions — ‘Temporary Labor Certification (TLC)’
rubrics_metrics.description: TLC means the certification made by the DOL OFLC Administrator, based on the CW-1 Application for Temporary Employment Certification and supporting documentation, with respect to an employer seeking to file a CW-1 petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: TLC is a prerequisite evidentiary determination by DOL regarding U.S. worker availability and wage impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions — ‘Transition period’ and ‘United States worker’
rubrics_metrics.description: Transition period means period beginning on the transition program effective date and ending Dec 31, 2029. United States worker means a U.S. citizen/national, an LPR, or certain Compact of Free Association citizens eligible for nonimmigrant admission and employment authorization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines temporal scope and who counts as U.S. worker for labor certification considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible aliens for CW-1 classification
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject to numerical limitation, an alien may be classified as CW-1 if, during the transition period, the alien: (i) will enter/remain in CNMI for employment in an occupational category designated by DHS; (ii) is petitioned for by an employer; (iii) is not present in the U.S., other than the CNMI; (iv) if present in the CNMI, is lawfully present; (v) is not inadmissible as a nonimmigrant or has been granted waivers of each applicable ground of inadmissibility; (vi) is ineligible for status in a nonimmigrant worker classification under section 101(a)(15) of the Act; and (vii) will not be employed in Construction and Extraction Occupations (SOC 47-0000) unless the alien is a long-term worker.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All listed eligibility conditions must be satisfied for CW-1 classification; construction exclusion applies absent long-term worker status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Derivative beneficiaries — CW-2 eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The spouse or minor child of a CW-1 may accompany or follow as CW-2 if: (i) the spouse/child is not present in the U.S., other than the CNMI; (ii) if present in CNMI, is lawfully present; and (iii) is not inadmissible as a nonimmigrant or has been granted a waiver of each applicable ground of inadmissibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Derivative eligibility mirrors principal's presence and admissibility requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible employers to petition for CW-1
rubrics_metrics.description: To be eligible to petition, an employer must: (i) be engaged in legitimate business; (ii) obtain a TLC from DOL and consider all available U.S. workers for the position; (iii) offer terms/conditions of employment consistent with the nature of the business and occupation in the CNMI; and (iv) comply with all Federal and Commonwealth employment-related requirements (nondiscrimination, occupational safety, minimum wage, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employer eligibility is contingent on legitimacy, DOL certification, appropriate employment terms, and compliance with labor laws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition filing requirements and fees for CW-1
rubrics_metrics.description: An employer seeking CW-1 classification must file a petition with USCIS and pay the requisite petition fee plus the CNMI education funding fee and the fraud prevention/detection fee as prescribed in 8 CFR part 106. If the beneficiary will perform services for more than one employer, each employer must file a separate petition with fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fees and separate-petition rule apply when multiple employers will employ the beneficiary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentary evidence and attestation requirements for CW petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition must be accompanied by documentary evidence establishing eligibility, including: (i) evidence that the petitioner meets the eligible employer definition; (ii) an attestation, certified true and accurate by an appropriate official, that the employer has not and will not displace a U.S. worker; is doing business as defined; is a legitimate business; is an eligible employer and will continue to comply; the beneficiary meets job qualifications; if present, beneficiary is lawfully present; the position is not temporary/seasonal nor reasonably believed to qualify for other nonimmigrant worker class; the position falls within DHS occupational categories; the petitioner will pay wage at least the greater of CNMI minimum wage, Federal minimum wage, or prevailing CNMI wage; and the petitioner will comply with reporting and retention requirements. Also requires (iii) evidence of licensure if occupation requires it, with rules on licensure, temporary licensure, and duties under supervision; and (iv) for petitions with start date on/after Oct 1, 2019, a TLC approved by DOL confirming insufficient U.S. workers and that employment will not adversely affect U.S. worker wages/conditions; if TLC accepts certain criteria, documentation that beneficiary qualifies per TLC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attestation contains many specific promises and factual claims; licensure pathways (full, temporary, supervised practice) are described; TLC is mandatory for later petitions and must match job qualifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Change of employers — maintaining CW-1 status
rubrics_metrics.description: A change to a new employer inconsistent with rules constitutes failure to maintain status. A CW-1 may change employers if: (i) the prospective new employer files a petition in accordance with petition requirements; and (ii) an extension of stay is requested if necessary. A CW-1 may work for a prospective new employer after the new employer files a nonfrivolous petition before the expiration of authorized stay, provided the CW-1 has not been employed without authorization after admission. Employment authorization continues until the new petition is adjudicated; if the new petition is denied, authorization ceases. If employment terminated prior to filing and a nonfrivolous petition is filed within 30 days, the CW-1 is not considered to be in violation during that 30-day period if other terms are complied with.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Change-of-employer is permitted only via timely-filed petitions; there is a 30-day grace in limited circumstances and authorization pendency rules apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amended or new petition requirement for material changes
rubrics_metrics.description: If there are material changes in the terms and conditions of employment, the petitioner must file an amended or new petition reflecting the changes. An amended or new petition must be submitted with a new TLC approved by DOL.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Material changes trigger fresh adjudication and require accompanying updated DOL certification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple beneficiaries in a single CW-1 petition
rubrics_metrics.description: An employer may include more than one beneficiary in a CW-1 petition if the beneficiaries will be working in the same occupational category, under the same terms and conditions, for the same period of time, and in the same location.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multi-beneficiary petitions allowed only when contemporaneous and identical job circumstances apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Named beneficiaries requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The petition must include the name of the beneficiary and other required information at the time of filing. Unnamed beneficiaries are not permitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All beneficiaries must be individually identified on filing; cannot leave names blank for later addition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Early termination employer obligation
rubrics_metrics.description: If an alien is dismissed before the end of the period of authorized admission, the petitioning employer must pay the reasonable cost of return transportation of the alien to the alien's last place of foreign residence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employer bears repatriation cost on early termination of employment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approval notice contents and processing constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: USCIS will consider all evidence and other required information to adjudicate the petition and will notify the petitioner of approval on Form I-797 or another form. The approval notice will include the CW-1 classification, name(s) of beneficiary(ies), and the petition's period of validity. A petition for multiple beneficiaries may be approved in whole or in part. The application for a TLC may not be filed with DOL earlier than 120 days before the date of actual need for initial petitions, or 180 days before expiration for extension petitions; the petition may be filed with USCIS after TLC approval. If DOL debars an employer from obtaining a TLC, USCIS may not approve future petitions during the debarment period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: TLC timing and DOL debarment consequences affect USCIS approval; approval notices state classification, beneficiaries, and validity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition validity periods
rubrics_metrics.description: An approved petition will be valid for up to one year, unless the beneficiary is a long-term worker in which case an approved petition will be valid for up to three years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard petition validity is one year; long-term workers get up to three-year petition validity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validity of Temporary Labor Certification (TLC)
rubrics_metrics.description: A TLC is valid only for the period of employment as approved on the CW-1 Application for Temporary Employment Certification. The TLC expires on the last day of authorized employment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: TLC's validity is coextensive with approved employment period and does not extend beyond it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures for applying for CW-1 or CW-2 status
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon petition approval, beneficiaries and eligible spouse/children outside the CNMI will be informed where to apply for visas authorizing admission in CW-1 or CW-2 status. If beneficiary is present in the CNMI, the petition also serves as the application for grant of CW-1 status. If eligible spouse/child are present, they may apply for CW-2 dependent status on Form I-539 (or alternative form) per instructions; CW-2 status may not be approved until CW-1 petition approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different procedural paths for beneficiaries inside vs outside CNMI and dependency approvals are contingent on principal petition approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biometrics and information submission
rubrics_metrics.description: The beneficiary of a CW-1 petition or the spouse/child applying for grant/extension/change to CW-2 must submit biometric information as requested by USCIS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Biometrics are required when requested and are part of adjudicative procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Period of admission for CW-1 and CW-2
rubrics_metrics.description: A CW-1 nonimmigrant will be admitted for the period of petition validity, plus up to 10 days before the validity period begins and 10 days after it ends. The CW-1 may not work except during petition validity. CW-2 spouse is admitted for same period as principal; CW-2 minor child likewise but not beyond the child's 18th birthday. Temporary departure from CNMI by principal will not affect derivative status provided relationship continues and principal remains eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Admission period includes short pre/post validity buffer; employment authorized only during validity; derivative durations tied to principal and subject to child's age limit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension of petition validity and stay
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitioner may request extension by filing a new petition only if original petition validity has not expired. Extensions may be granted for up to 1 year (or up to 3 years for long-term workers) until end of transition period, subject to numerical limitation. To qualify for extension the petitioner must demonstrate the beneficiary continuously maintained CW-1 terms, remains admissible to the U.S., and remains eligible for CW-1 classification. A non-long-term beneficiary may not be granted CW-1 status beyond three consecutive petition validity periods unless the beneficiary departed and remained outside the U.S. for at least 30 continuous days after expiration of the third period before filing a new petition. The derivative CW-2 may file Form I-539 for extension; CW-2 extension may not be approved until CW-1 extension petition approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensions require continuous compliance, admissibility, eligibility, and are limited cumulatively; a 30-day outside-U.S. break is required after three consecutive petition periods before new petitioning for non-long-term workers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Change or adjustment of status for CW nonimmigrants
rubrics_metrics.description: A CW-1 or CW-2 nonimmigrant can apply to change nonimmigrant status under section 248 or apply for adjustment of status under section 245 if otherwise eligible. During the transition period, CW-1 or CW-2 nonimmigrants may be beneficiary of or apply for any nonimmigrant or immigrant visa classification for which they qualify.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CW-classified persons retain ability to seek change/adjustment if qualifying, subject to general statutory requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of filing for permanent labor certification/immigrant petition or adjustment on CW status
rubrics_metrics.description: Filing or approval of a permanent labor certification, immigrant visa preference petition, or an application for adjustment of status, or lack of residence abroad, will not be a basis for denying: (i) a CW-1 petition filed on behalf of the alien; (ii) a request to extend CW-1 status pursuant to a petition previously filed; (iii) an application for CW-2 classification filed by an alien; (iv) a request to extend CW-2 status related to a CW-1 extension; or (v) an application for admission as a CW-1 or CW-2 nonimmigrant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concurrent pursuit of permanent residence-related filings does not by itself disqualify CW petitions, extensions, or CW-2 applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection of petitions due to numerical limitation
rubrics_metrics.description: USCIS may reject an employer's petition for new or extended CW-1 status if any numerical limitation has been met. In that case, petition and fee will be rejected and returned with notice that numbers are unavailable for the CW classification. The beneficiary's application for admission based upon an approved petition will not be rejected based upon the numerical limitation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rejection (not denial) occurs when cap exhausted; fees returned; previously approved petition-based admissions are not retroactively affected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Denial of CW petitions or status and appeals
rubrics_metrics.description: Ultimate decision to grant or deny CW-1 or CW-2 classification or status is discretionary; petition/application may be denied for failure to demonstrate eligibility or for other good cause. Denial of a petition to classify an alien as CW-1 may be appealed to the USCIS Administrative Appeals Office or successor. Denial of CW-1 or CW-2 status within the CNMI, or of a change/extension of status filed under this section, may not be appealed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguishes between appealable petition denials (appeal to AAO) versus nonappealable in-CNMI status denials/denials of change/extension within CNMI.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terms and conditions of CW nonimmigrant status — geographical limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: CW-1 and CW-2 statuses are only applicable in the CNMI. Entry, employment and residence in the rest of the United States (including Guam) require the appropriate visa or visa waiver and nonimmigrant classification. Except as provided for direct Guam transit, entering or attempting to enter other parts of the U.S. without appropriate visa/waiver or violating conditions of nonimmigrant stay in other parts of the U.S. will be deemed to have violated CW status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CW status is territorially limited to CNMI; travel or activity outside CNMI generally jeopardizes status absent specific exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terms and conditions — re-entry rules
rubrics_metrics.description: An alien with CW-1 or CW-2 status who travels abroad from the CNMI will require a CW-1 or CW-2 or other appropriate visa to be re-admitted to the CNMI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Re-admission to CNMI after foreign travel requires valid visa; maintain documentary proof for return.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terms and conditions — travel outside the CNMI / direct Guam transit
rubrics_metrics.description: (A) Direct Guam transit from the CNMI: an alien with CW-1/CW-2 may travel to a foreign place via a direct Guam transit without being deemed to violate status. (B) Travel from a foreign place to the CNMI: an alien with a valid CW visa, admissible to CNMI, may be admitted to the U.S. in Guam for the purpose of direct Guam transit to the CNMI. An alien who violates the terms of direct Guam transit violates CW status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Direct Guam transit is narrowly defined and permitted; violations of transit terms can cause status violations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terms and conditions — employment authorization limitations for CW-1
rubrics_metrics.description: An alien with CW-1 status is authorized employment only in the CNMI and only for the petitioning employer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CW-1 employment is employer- and location-specific; unauthorized employment or work outside CNMI or for another employer violates status.
